messages:
Diego: Quick design review — pushed a Figma prototype for the prompt-sets / evals panel. Two main views: a compact scorecard list with inline regression diffs, and a modal-based approval flow for prompt set changes. TL;DR: want feedback on density, keyboard/a11y, and the approval microcopy. link: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx

Asha: Nice. Scorecard layout looks clean. My main callout is density — too many columns on small widths. Also a11y: need proper focus indicators and contrast on the diff chips.

Ben: Agreed on contrast. Also ensure keyboard nav across rows + expand/collapse works. On mobile, we should collapse into a stacked view.

Priya: From product side — we need the ability to mark a prompt set as "requires approval" and to attach a test-suite so CI can gate deploys. Also the approval modal should show the exact regression diffs that triggered the review (not just scores).

Eva: I added a variant that collapses long prompt text into a 3-line preview with a "view full" affordance. For diffs I proposed a tiny sparkline + +/- delta next to the score, and an expandable diff panel for examples.

ci-bot: ci-bot: visual snapshot tests failing on the scorecard list for the narrow breakpoint. Snapshot id: vs-2026-03-21-09

Diego: I'll look at the narrow breakpoint snapshots. Question for UX: do we truncate prompt text with ellipses or wrap to multiple lines? Truncation saves vertical space but hides context.

Asha: Prefer wrap but limit to 3 lines with an explicit "more" control to avoid layout thrash. Use CSS `line-clamp` where supported and fall back to fade gradient + "more" button.

Ben: Example CSS for line clamp (put in the component):
```css
.prompt-preview {
  display: -webkit-box;
  -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```
Don't forget to include a visible keyboard target for the "more" control.

Priya: For the approval flow: propose states: draft -> review -> approved -> released. Reviewer must be able to add a changelog entry. If regression delta > X% require two reviewers. Can we make that configurable per workspace?

Diego: Sounds good. We'll add policy config in the backend. UX question: should approvals be inline on the scorecard row or a separate modal? I lean modal for larger diffs and keyboard focus management.

Eva: Modal is fine. A few accessibility nits: focus trap, role=dialog + aria-labelledby, announce modal open with aria-live and provide skip link to raw examples. Also ensure the diff list is navigable by screen reader (use headings for each example).

Asha: Also add an aria-live region that summarizes the regression delta when a set is selected, e.g., "Prompt Set X has +12% regression on helpfulness compared to baseline." This helps screen reader users understand impact quickly.

Priya: I'll update the ticket with the gating rules and request the backend flag. Also we should update docs: how to interpret the sparkline and delta numbers — small copy tweak.

Diego: I'll iterate the figma and address the narrow breakpoint snapshots. Will add keyboard / focus states and aria attributes.

qa-bot: qa-bot: created ticket PROD-2123 for e2e accessibility tests (keyboard nav + screen reader smoke). Assigned to @Ben and @Asha.

Ben: I'll take the e2e tests. Quick note: for the scorecard filters (by regression, by test-suite) we need to preserve state in URL so bookmarks and deep links work.

Eva: Added microcopy suggestions in Figma comments: change "Approve" button label to "Approve and Release?" only when auto-release is enabled; otherwise "Approve" with secondary "Release now" action.

Asha: :thumbsup: Also let's make the diff chips have accessible color alternatives (icon + text) not just color.

Diego: Great. I'll push an updated Figma file and a small PR for the narrow breakpoint CSS. Expect a follow-up with screenshots and updated snapshot ids. Thanks everyone!
